label: input q at original position 3 or 4
explanation: Fires only on the letter q as an input during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase. On dev, every q input at original position 3 or 4 is active (precision 1.0), with typical activation 0.5-0.95 of max. There is a weak tail on q at positions 2 and 5 (usually under ~0.15 of max, 0.8% of mass), and nothing at positions 0-1 or 6+. It never fires on any other token, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase (including when q is fed back as an output). Mass splits about 58% at t=3 and 42% at t=4. Repeated q (not its first occurrence) shows up among lower activations, but I did not quantify this.

issues: The misses are not random noise: all 1840 test misses (0.8% of mass, about 5.8% of active steps) are q inputs at t=2 or t=5, mostly 0.05-0.11 of max. The explanation already says this, and widening the predicate to t in 2..5 makes things worse (test P 0.555, R 1.0, F1 0.713). So the current predicate is still the best one.

Every factual claim checks out on dev. Mass by t: 0.577 at t=3, 0.415 at t=4, 0.005 at t=2, 0.003 at t=5. Activation is zero at t=0,1 and at t>=6, zero on the delimiter, zero in the copy phase, and zero on every token except q. On test there are 0 false positives.

The note about repeated q is slightly misleading. q at t=3/4 that comes after an earlier q still always fires (test precision 1.0, 3338 steps, 10.6% of mass), so repeats do not suppress the feature. Their share of activations matches their share of mass, so there is no clear magnitude drop either.
